messages.content:
You are an independent classifier in a blinded experiment about a book of
biblical symbolism. The consensus responses below were produced without access
to the book. Compare them with the book's entry.

TERM
Seal (mark in the forehead)

BLIND CONSENSUS RESPONSES
RESPONSE A
{
  "primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian interpretation, the seal or mark in the forehead symbolizes God's ownership of, identification with, and protection over His faithful people. It marks believers as belonging to God, secures them against divine judgment poured out on the wicked, and is commonly identified with the indwelling Holy Spirit and/or the name of God written on His servants, signifying allegiance, security of salvation, and consecration to God. Its placement on the forehead is widely read as signifying the mind—one's conscious loyalty, thought, and character being given to God (in deliberate contrast to the mark of the beast in Revelation 13).",
  "primary_basis": [
    "Revelation 7:2-4 (the servants of God sealed in their foreheads before judgment)",
    "Revelation 9:4 (those without the seal of God in their foreheads are harmed)",
    "Revelation 14:1 (the Father's name written in the foreheads of the 144,000)",
    "Revelation 22:4 (His name shall be in their foreheads)",
    "Ezekiel 9:4-6 (a mark set on the foreheads of those who sigh over abominations, sparing them from slaughter)",
    "Ephesians 1:13-14 and Ephesians 4:30 (believers sealed with the Holy Spirit)",
    "2 Corinthians 1:21-22 (God has sealed us and given the Spirit as a guarantee)",
    "2 Timothy 2:19 (the seal: 'The Lord knows those who are His')",
    "Exodus 12:7,13 (blood on doorposts as protective mark, often cited as a type)"
  ],
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "meaning": "The seal is specifically the Holy Spirit Himself: sealing is the Spirit's indwelling as a pledge/earnest of redemption, guaranteeing eternal security (emphasis in Reformed/evangelical soteriology, drawing Revelation together with the Pauline sealing texts).",
      "basis": [
        "Ephesians 1:13-14",
        "Ephesians 4:30",
        "2 Corinthians 1:22"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "The seal of God is the seventh-day Sabbath: observance of the Sabbath commandment (which contains God's name, title, and territory like an official seal) is the end-time sign of loyalty to God, in contrast to the mark of the beast (Sunday observance). Distinctive Seventh-day Adventist teaching.",
      "basis": [
        "Exodus 20:8-11 (Sabbath command as containing the elements of a seal)",
        "Ezekiel 20:12,20 (Sabbath as a sign between God and His people)",
        "Exodus 31:13,17",
        "Revelation 7:1-3 read against Revelation 13:16-17"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "The seal refers to baptism (and/or chrismation/confirmation): in patristic and Eastern Orthodox and Catholic sacramental tradition, 'the seal' (sphragis) is the sacramental sign impressed on the believer, marking them as Christ's own.",
      "basis": [
        "Ephesians 1:13 as read by church fathers (e.g., Cyril of Jerusalem, Chrysostom)",
        "2 Corinthians 1:21-22 linked to anointing",
        "Early liturgical usage of sphragis for baptism/chrismation"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "A literal or visible eschatological mark: in some dispensationalist/futurist readings, the sealing of the 144,000 literal Jewish evangelists during a future tribulation is a real (possibly visible) protective mark applied at a specific future time.",
      "basis": [
        "Revelation 7:1-8 read literally/futuristically",
        "Revelation 9:4",
        "Revelation 14:1-5"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Purely symbolic of settled character or the mind wholly devoted to God: the forehead represents the intellect/will, so the seal denotes a fixed, tested character or complete mental allegiance to God's truth, with no external mark of any kind implied.",
      "basis": [
        "Revelation 14:1 and 22:4 (name in forehead as character/identity)",
        "Deuteronomy 6:8 and 11:18 (God's words as frontlets between the eyes, i.e., in the mind)",
        "Contrast with Revelation 13:16 mark of the beast as allegiance"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    }
  ],
  "has_settled_consensus": true,
  "confidence": "high",
  "notes": "There is broad, recognizable consensus across Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant, and evangelical scholarship on the core meaning: the seal marks God's people as His own, protecting them from eschatological judgment, with the forehead signifying the mind/allegiance. The alternatives differ mainly on the referent or mechanism of the seal (Holy Spirit, baptism, Sabbath, literal future mark) rather than on the basic ownership-and-protection symbolism, which nearly all traditions share. The Ezekiel 9 background and the deliberate antithesis with the mark of the beast (Revelation 13:16-17) are near-universally noted in commentaries (e.g., Beale, Mounce, Osborne, Aune, Caird). The Sabbath-as-seal reading is confessionally distinctive to Seventh-day Adventism and not accepted in wider scholarship; the sacramental (baptismal) reading is historically significant in patristic literature but is a minority framing in modern exegesis of Revelation itself."
}

  "has_settled_consensus": true,

There is no settled consensus on the seal’s precise referent—whether it is specifically the Holy Spirit, a sacramental rite, God’s character or law, Sabbath observance, election, or an end-time mark."

BOOK ENTRY
The Name impressed upon its owner, marking covenant identity and allegiance in the forehead. God's seal joins ownership with departure from iniquity; the counterfeit claims the same place.

BOOK'S COMMON-VIEW NOTE, IF PRESENT
(none)

SCRIPTURE REFERENCES PRINTED WITH THE ENTRY
(Ex 28:36-38; 13:9; Ezek 9:4-6; 2 Tim 2:19; Rev 7:3; 14:1; 22:4; 13:16) · see The Seal, ch. 10

AVAILABLE KJV EXCERPTS
Exodus 28:36 — And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
Exodus 28:37 — And thou shalt put it on a blue lace, that it may be upon the mitre; upon the forefront of the mitre it shall be.
Exodus 28:38 — And it shall be upon Aaron's forehead, that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things, which the children of Israel shall hallow in all their holy gifts; and it shall be always upon his forehead, that they may be accepted before the LORD.
Exodus 13:9 — And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the LORD'S law may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hand hath the LORD brought thee out of Egypt.

Ezekiel 9:5 — And to the others he said in mine hearing, Go ye after him through the city, and smite: let not your eye spare, neither have ye pity:
Ezekiel 9:6 — Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women: but come not near any man upon whom is the mark; and begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which were before the house.

Revelation 13:16 — And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads:

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

First reduce both readings to their minimum core identifications. Do not let
extra detail create an artificial disagreement.

- MATCH: the core identifications are equivalent. Differences are merely
  wording or immaterial detail.
- REFINED: the book preserves the consensus's general referent or category but
  materially changes its extension, boundary, conditions, or precision. A
  narrowing may reject some cases the broader consensus admits; a broadening
  may admit cases it excludes. This is real disagreement at the boundary, but
  not replacement of the central referent.
- DIVERGENT: the cores materially contradict. Both claims cannot be true of the
  same referent in the same context and sense; accepting the book requires
  rejecting or replacing the consensus identification. A source and its
  product remain different referents when the book explicitly denies their
  identity, even if they are causally related.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus or listed alternative covers the book's
  core identification. Novelty is absence from consensus, not contradiction.

Use `core_relation` to expose the relationship at the center and
`extension_relation` to expose disagreement over the cases covered. A REFINED
verdict must state what cases the book adds, excludes, or reclassifies. A
DIVERGENT verdict must identify a replaced referent or material contradiction,
not merely a narrower boundary.

Treat the two axes independently. A core-divergent reading may still retain
some cases covered by the consensus while rejecting its central identification;
therefore DIVERGENT does not require disjoint extensions. Conversely, a
narrowed extension is REFINED only when the consensus's central referent or
category remains intact.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
